candidate.answerReason: Substitution gives \(x^2=12/7\), which has two distinct real roots. Each determines exactly one intersection because \(y=x\).

methods.label: Substitute and count real roots
methods.explanation: Substitution gives \((1/4+1/3)x^2=1\), that is, \(7x^2/12=1\). There are 2 real roots, so there are 2 intersection points.
methods.levelReason: Uses substitution and the two real square roots of a positive number, requiring only elementary school algebra.
